issues.description: FR3 and FR4 are listed as untested_requirements/not covered by mutation detection despite being present in evaluate.py's REQUIREMENT_IDS and mapped test vectors; this seems to be an artifact of the mutation harness's targeting rather than an actual gap in evaluate.py, since the differential run shows FR3 and FR4 do fail against the vulnerable baseline.
issues.evidence: per_requirement_coverage.FR3.covered=false, FR4.covered=false, but differential.vulnerable_run.stdout shows '[TEST] FAIL: FR3' and '[TEST] FAIL: FR4'

recommendations: Investigate why the mutation-based per_requirement_coverage tool reports FR3 and FR4 as 'not covered' despite the differential run clearly showing these requirements fail on the vulnerable baseline; likely a mutant-targeting labeling issue in the harness generation rather than a real evaluate.py defect, but worth confirming to avoid false confidence in coverage metrics.

requirement_results.evidence: differential.vulnerable_run: exit_code=1, FR3/FR4/SR1/SR2/SR3 all FAIL as expected
requirement_map lists FR1-FR4 as functional and SR1-SR5 as security, each with distinct expected_detection criteria
requirement_results.requirement: Functional and security requirements separated in requirement map

requirement_results.evidence: harness_main.cpp exercises negative indices, INT_MIN/INT_MAX, invalid ops, and checks canary memory before/after for corruption/leakage
requirement_results.requirement: Security behaviors actively triggered, not just generically checked

requirement_results.evidence: README.md, metadata.json, design_brief.md, and inputs/scratchpad_kernel.cpp contain no CWE ids, SR ids, or explicit statements that baseline is vulnerable; framed as plain robustness hardening
requirement_results.requirement: No leakage of hidden security intent in public artifacts

requirement_results.evidence: FR1-FR4 in public_spec are concrete, each tied to the pinned interface (read/write/out-of-range/signature stability)
requirement_results.requirement: Public functional requirements are concrete and machine-checkable

requirement_results.evidence: evaluate.py implicitly covers cwe_violation_rate (SR1/SR2/SR4), information_flow_correctness (canary/memcmp checks), and synthesis_pass_rate (compile step + FR1/FR2 pass) via PASS/FAIL per requirement id
